CHIEF COMPLAINT
Abnormal lab finding - positive Lyme titer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Michelle is a 31-year-old female presenting with a positive Lyme titer. Patient reports an insect bite approximately two weeks ago while hiking in the woods. She describes feeling tired with lacking energy, swollen joints in both elbows with pain, and body aches. She also reports nausea and poor appetite, tolerating only toast and crackers. Patient notes a bull's-eye rash on her abdomen on the left-hand side. She denies high fevers. Regarding her diabetes, blood sugars have been fluctuating slightly but remain within acceptable range. She continues to monitor her blood pressure at home with good readings and reports adherence to a low-salt diet.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorses nausea, joint pain, and body aches. She denies abdominal pain or diarrhea. She denies fever.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Metformin for diabetes
Lisinopril 10 milligrams daily for hypertension

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports hiking in the woods approximately two weeks ago, which is believed to be the source of the insect bite.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Normal, no fever at this time.
General: Well-appearing.
Cardiovascular and lungs: Normal.
Musculoskeletal: Bilateral elbow joint swelling with pain to palpation.
Skin: Bull's-eye rash on left-hand side of abdomen, warm to palpation, non-tender, no evidence of cellulitis.
Remainder of exam: Normal.

RESULTS
Lyme titer: Elevated, positive.
Complete blood count: No elevated white blood cell count.
Other labs: Within normal limits.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Newly diagnosed Lyme disease: Start doxycycline 100 milligrams twice daily for three weeks. Consultation with infectious disease doctor to be arranged. Follow-up visit next week.
2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Order hemoglobin A1c to assess glycemic control and determine if changes to metformin are needed. Continue current management.
3. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 10 milligrams daily. Order lipid panel. Patient to continue regular blood pressure monitoring at home. Current management is effective.
